approachQuestion.prompt:
Shift the Duty Roster

Rotate an integer array roster to the right by k positions in place. A right shift sends the last element to the front; shifting by the length restores the original order. Return nothing and keep the same array storage.

Example 1: roster=[2,4,6,8,10], k=2 → [8,10,2,4,6].
Example 2: roster=[7,9,1], k=6 → [7,9,1].
Example 3: roster=[5], k=13 → [5].

Constraints:
1 ≤ n=roster.length ≤ 200,000; 0 ≤ k ≤ 10^9.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Equal values remain separate entries.
The array may be overwritten but must not be replaced or resized.
constraints: Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Equal values remain separate entries.
The array may be overwritten but must not be replaced or resized.

options.text: Set s=k mod n. If s=0, stop. Otherwise reverse the whole array, then reverse its first s elements and its remaining n−s elements. Implement each reversal by swapping inward from its two ends.
options.feedback: Whole-array reversal brings the old suffix to the front but reverses each part internally. Reversing the two parts restores their internal order, producing exactly the required right rotation.

options.text: Set s=k mod n. Copy the whole input into a helper array, then assign roster[(i+s) mod n]=copy[i] for every original index i.
options.feedback: This rotates correctly and preserves the roster’s storage, but the full helper copy is removable with the reversal method.

options.text: Set s=k mod n. For i from 0 through n−1, assign roster[(i+s) mod n]=roster[i], reading from the currently changing array.
options.feedback: A write can destroy a source not yet read. For [1,2,3], k=1, the first write replaces 2 with 1 and later reads no longer contain all original values.

options.text: Set s=k mod n. Reverse the first s elements, then the remaining n−s elements, then the whole array.
options.feedback: This performs a left rotation by s rather than a right rotation. For [1,2,3,4,5], k=2, it gives [3,4,5,1,2], but the required result is [4,5,1,2,3].

feedback.reason: Reduce oversized shifts modulo n before performing any movement.
details: Reduce k modulo the nonzero array length and stop for a zero shift. Reverse the whole array, then reverse the first s positions and the remaining suffix, using inward swaps for each reversal.

Reduce oversized shifts modulo n before performing any movement. Reversing the whole roster moves the final block forward but reverses both blocks internally; reversing the two blocks restores their internal order. Handle an empty roster before modulo, and return directly for a zero reduced shift.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Reverse the Whole Roster and Then Both Parts”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be roster.length. Analyze the worst case over legal k and arrays of length n, including the possibility that some k give an immediate return. Modulo on these bounded integers and array swaps cost constant time. Input is mutated storage and there is no returned storage. Include helper indices, one swap temporary and stack. Reversals are iterative; no recursion, hashing or helper array is used.
constraints: Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Equal values remain separate entries.
The array may be overwritten but must not be replaced or resized.

options.text: O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space for every k.

feedback.reason: Three bounded reversal scans use constant swap state.
details: For a nonzero reduced shift, the three reversal ranges have total length 2n, so their swaps take linear time. Only indices and one temporary value are used. Some shifts return immediately, but this does not change the worst-case bound over k.
The option “O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Three bounded reversal scans rotate in place using fixed helper state.
The option “O(k*n + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This reflects repeatedly shifting single positions, not modulo reduction followed by three reversals.
The option “O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.”: A copied source would require this auxiliary space, but the fixed method makes no copy.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space for every k.”: Nonzero shifts of a growing roster require swaps across the array.
